questions.question: A marketer must hit a 4:1 ROAS target on a 75,000-peso Meta ads budget. How much tracked revenue must the campaign generate?
questions.explanation: ROAS = revenue / ad spend, so required revenue = 4 x 75,000 = 300,000 pesos.

questions.question: A funnel strategy maps creative to four jobs: grab attention, build interest, create desire, then prompt action. Which classic model is this?
questions.explanation: Attention-Interest-Desire-Action is the AIDA sequence describing how messaging moves a prospect toward purchase.

questions.question: An ad network keeps serving hiking-boot ads to a shopper because cookies reveal she spent the week browsing trail-gear sites. Which targeting method is this?
questions.explanation: Behavioral targeting profiles users from their observed browsing activity rather than page context or demographics.

questions.question: A store spent 120,000 pesos on sales and marketing last month and gained 300 new customers. What is its CAC?
questions.explanation: CAC = total acquisition spend / new customers = 120,000 / 300 = 400 pesos per customer.

questions.question: A subscriber pays 500 pesos monthly and stays an average of 24 months. Ignoring costs, what is this customer's CLV?
questions.explanation: CLV = average monthly spend x lifespan = 500 x 24 = 12,000 pesos.

questions.question: After a checkout redesign lifts the purchase rate from 2.0% to 2.6%, the team keeps A/B-testing each page element to push it higher. What discipline are they practicing?
questions.explanation: Conversion rate optimization is the systematic testing of page elements to raise the share of visitors who convert.

questions.question: Under a linear attribution model, a buyer touched 4 channels before an 8,000-peso purchase. How much revenue credit does the email touchpoint get?
questions.explanation: Linear attribution splits credit equally: 8,000 / 4 touchpoints = 2,000 pesos (25%) for email.

questions.question: A skincare brand pays a popular TikTok creator to demonstrate its products to her two million followers. What marketing approach is this?
questions.explanation: Influencer marketing leverages a creator's audience trust and reach to promote products, typically for fees or commission.

questions.question: New subscribers automatically get a welcome email on day 0, a tips email on day 3, and a discount offer on day 7. What is this scheduled email sequence called?
questions.explanation: A drip campaign sends a pre-written series of messages on a schedule, 'dripping' content to nurture leads over time.

questions.question: Instead of hand-setting CPCs, an advertiser lets Google Ads adjust each auction bid in real time to maximize conversions. What bidding strategy is this?
questions.explanation: Smart Bidding is Google's machine-learning bid automation that optimizes per auction for conversions or conversion value.

questions.question: A buyer sees a display ad, taps a social post, then converts through a search ad — and the reporting model gives 100% credit to the search ad. Which model is this?
questions.explanation: Last-click attribution assigns the entire conversion value to the final touchpoint before purchase, ignoring earlier assists.

questions.question: On the same journey — display ad, social post, then search ad — a different model credits the display ad fully because it introduced the customer. Which model?
questions.explanation: First-click attribution assigns all credit to the initial touchpoint, valuing the channel that started the relationship.

questions.question: Of 200 shoppers who added to cart, 50 completed purchase. What is the cart-to-purchase conversion rate?
questions.explanation: 50 divided by 200 equals 25%.

questions.question: An A/B tool reports the variant beat control with p = 0.03. Does this clear the conventional 95% confidence bar for declaring a winner?
questions.explanation: p = 0.03 means under 5% chance of a false positive, clearing the standard 95% significance threshold (p < 0.05).

questions.question: A store booked 450,000 pesos in revenue across 1,500 orders last month. What is its average order value?
questions.explanation: AOV = revenue / orders = 450,000 / 1,500 = 300 pesos per order.

questions.question: A store spends 50,000 pesos on Meta ads and earns 250,000 pesos in tracked revenue. What is its ROAS?
questions.explanation: ROAS = revenue / ad spend = 250,000 / 50,000 = 5, i.e., five pesos earned per peso spent.

questions.question: Of 8,000 site sessions, 240 ended in a purchase. What is the conversion rate?
questions.explanation: Conversion rate = 240 / 8,000 = 0.03 = 3%.

questions.question: Of 1,500 carts created, 1,050 were abandoned before checkout. What is the cart abandonment rate?
questions.explanation: Abandonment rate = 1,050 / 1,500 = 0.70 = 70%.

questions.question: An affiliate partner is paid 200 pesos only when a referred visitor actually completes a purchase. Which pricing model is this?
questions.explanation: CPA (cost per action/acquisition) pays only on a completed conversion, unlike CPC or CPM.

questions.question: 25,000 marketing emails were delivered and 1,250 recipients clicked a link. What is the click-through rate?
questions.explanation: CTR = 1,250 clicks / 25,000 delivered = 5%.
